route_name: Persian Gulf to India via Strait of Hormuz
primary_corridor: Persian Gulf - Strait of Hormuz - Gulf of Oman - Arabian Sea
corridor_evidence: EIA states the Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea and carried about 20 million b/d in 2024
source: EnergyShield-AI Phase 1 analyst-defined corridor (MODELLED - not an observed shipment record)
notes: MODELLED CORRIDOR. This row asserts that a plausible physical routing exists between these nodes; it does NOT assert that any cargo currently moves on it, nor any volume, frequency or commercial availability. origin_port is null because no Saudi Gulf-coast export terminal was named in the sources consulted. destination_port is a MODELLING CHOICE (a representative Indian west-coast crude-receiving port from ports.csv), not a property of the corridor. estimated_distance_km and estimated_transit_days are null - to be modelled later; no sourced figure exists and none was invented.

route_name: United Arab Emirates to India via Fujairah
corridor_evidence: ADNOC states it is 'currently exporting from the UAE's Fujairah and Jebel Dhanna ports to countries such as Japan, China, South Korea, Thailand, and India'
source: EnergyShield-AI Phase 1 analyst-defined corridor (MODELLED - not an observed shipment record)
notes: MODELLED CORRIDOR, but with direct corridor evidence: ADNOC names India as a destination served from Fujairah. chokepoints_involved is deliberately EMPTY, and that is the analytical point of this corridor - Fujairah sits on the Gulf of Oman OUTSIDE the Strait of Hormuz, so this routing does not transit CP001. A route from the UAE's other named terminal, Jebel Dhanna, WOULD transit Hormuz; the two must not be conflated. estimated_distance_km and estimated_transit_days are null - to be modelled later.

route_name: Saudi Arabia to India via Yanbu and the Red Sea
primary_corridor: Red Sea - Bab el-Mandeb - Gulf of Aden - Arabian Sea
corridor_evidence: EIA describes Yanbu as Saudi Arabia's primary crude oil export terminal on the Red Sea, and records Aramco beginning to export Arab Heavy from Yanbu in early 2024
source: EnergyShield-AI Phase 1 analyst-defined corridor (MODELLED - not an observed shipment record)
notes: MODELLED CORRIDOR. A Red Sea departure from Yanbu reaches the Indian Ocean southbound through Bab el-Mandeb (CP002) and therefore does NOT transit the Suez Canal, which lies north of Yanbu. This is the Hormuz-avoiding Saudi corridor and is the counterpart to RT001. destination_port is a modelling choice. estimated_distance_km and estimated_transit_days are null - to be modelled later.

route_name: Mediterranean to India via Suez Canal and SUMED
primary_corridor: Mediterranean Sea - Suez Canal or SUMED pipeline - Red Sea - Bab el-Mandeb - Arabian Sea
corridor_evidence: EIA states the Suez Canal connects the Red Sea and the Gulf of Suez with the Mediterranean Sea, and that the SUMED pipeline is the only alternate route between the Red Sea and the Mediterranean
source: EnergyShield-AI Phase 1 analyst-defined corridor (MODELLED - not an observed shipment record)
notes: MODELLED CORRIDOR. DIRECTION NOTE: the Phase 1 brief lists this corridor as 'Red Sea -> Suez/SUMED -> Mediterranean -> India'. Taken literally that is northbound to the Mediterranean and then away from India. It is modelled here in the INDIA-INBOUND direction (Mediterranean southbound through Suez or SUMED into the Red Sea, then through Bab el-Mandeb to the Arabian Sea), which is the only orientation in which it terminates in India. origin_country and origin_supplier_id are null: this corridor is defined by its transit segment, not by a single origin country. CP003 and CP004 are ALTERNATIVES to each other for the same segment, not sequential legs - the route_nodes sequence records the canal branch. estimated_distance_km and estimated_transit_days are null - to be modelled later.

source: EnergyShield-AI Phase 1 analyst-defined corridor (MODELLED - not an observed shipment record)
notes: MODELLED CORRIDOR WITH THE LEAST SUPPORT IN THIS DATASET. corridor_evidence and corridor_evidence_url are NULL: no authoritative source describing a Russia-to-India crude routing was obtained within Phase 1. primary_corridor is 'not determined' and chokepoints_involved is empty because Russian crude can reach India by several materially different paths - from Baltic or Black Sea ports via Suez or via the Cape of Good Hope, or from Pacific ports with no chokepoint of this list at all - and choosing one without a source would be a fabrication. origin_port is null for the same reason. This row is a placeholder for a corridor that Phase 2 must resolve into distinct routings; it must NOT be treated as a single physical path. estimated_distance_km and estimated_transit_days are null - to be modelled later.
